stories.headline: Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI Unveil $25B Terafab Chip Factory Targeting 1 Terawatt Annual Output

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk officially launched the Terafab project on March 21 at the defunct Seaholm Power Plant in Austin, Texas — a $25 billion joint venture between Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI to build the largest chip fabrication facility ever, consolidating chip design, lithography, fabrication, memory production, advanced packaging, and testing under one roof.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk took the stage at the defunct Seaholm Power Plant in Austin on March 21 to officially launch the project, calling it 'the most epic chip building exercise in history by far.'

key_facts.fact: Terafab targets 2-nanometer process technology with an initial output of 100,000 wafer starts per month, scaling to 1 million wafer starts — roughly 70% of TSMC's entire current global output — and producing 100 to 200 billion custom AI and memory chips annually.
key_facts.excerpt: Terafab is designed for an initial output of 100,000 wafer starts per month, with ambitions to scale to 1 million wafer starts per month at full capacity. For context, that full-scale target would represent roughly 70% of TSMC's entire current global output.

key_facts.fact: Tesla's fifth-generation AI5 chip, the first product Terafab is designed to produce, delivers a 50x total improvement over the AI4 generation with 10x raw compute increase and 9x memory capacity. A separate D3 chip will be built specifically for SpaceX's orbital satellite constellation.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla claims its new AI5 chip delivers a 50x total improvement over the previous AI4 generation, with 10x raw compute increase and 9x memory capacity.

key_facts.fact: Musk stated that 80% of Terafab's output will be directed toward space-based orbital AI satellites, with 20% for terrestrial applications including Tesla robotaxis and Optimus humanoid robots, which alone require 100–200 GW of chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk's stated goal is one terawatt of computing power annually, split between Tesla's AI5 inference chips for vehicles and Optimus robots, and D3 chips built specifically for SpaceXAI's orbital satellite constellation.

key_facts.fact: Musk framed the project as essential, saying current global fabrication produces only 2% of what his companies require and warning that chip supply from TSMC, Samsung, and Micron will hit a ceiling within 3–4 years.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk acknowledged: 'We're very grateful to our existing supply chain, to Samsung, TSMC, Micron and others,' adding 'but there's a maximum rate at which they're comfortable expanding... we need the chips, so we're going to build the Terafab.'

key_facts.fact: Analysts are skeptical: Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon said 'I suspect this is actually harder than sending rockets to Mars,' and Electrek compared the announcement to Tesla's Battery Day 2020 promises, noting the 4680 battery cell program achieved only ~2% of original volume goals.
key_facts.excerpt: Stacy Rasgon (Bernstein): 'It's Musk, so I would never count it out. But I suspect this is actually harder than sending rockets to Mars.'

stories.headline: SpaceX Reveals AI Sat Mini Specs: 170m Satellites With 100kW for Million-Unit Orbital Data Center

key_facts.fact: At the March 21 Terafab event in Austin, Musk showed an illustration of the 'AI Sat Mini' satellite that will initially power SpaceX's orbital data center constellation. Each satellite stretches over 170 meters when deployed — roughly 50% longer than a Starship V3 — and generates approximately 100 kW of solar power dedicated to onboard AI processors.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk showed an illustration of an 'AI Sat Mini' that he said would initially be used in the constellation. Each satellite would provide 100 kilowatts of power for AI processors on board.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX filed an FCC application in late January 2026 for a constellation of up to one million satellites to function as an orbital data center for AI applications. The January filing provided few technical details; the March 21 event was the first time Musk disclosed satellite dimensions and power specs.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX filed an application with the Federal Communications Commission in late January for a constellation of up to one million satellites that would be used as an orbital data center for AI applications. The company provided few technical details about the constellation, including the size of the satellites, in that application.

key_facts.fact: Future satellite iterations are targeting the megawatt power range — a 10x increase over the current 100 kW design. The annual compute target is 100 GW added per year, with a path to 1 TW total orbital AI compute capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's new 'AI Sat Mini' satellite stretches over 170 meters when deployed — roughly 50% longer than a Starship V3 — and is designed to generate approximately 100 kW of solar power per unit, with future iterations targeting the Megawatt range.

key_facts.fact: Musk said the Terafab chips are the 'missing ingredient' for the orbital data center plan, stating: 'We either build the Terafab or we don't have the chips, and we need the chips, so we're going to build the Terafab.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We either build the Terafab or we don't have the chips, and we need the chips, so we're going to build the Terafab,' he said.

key_facts.fact: Amazon filed a formal objection to SpaceX's million-satellite plan on March 6, calling the FCC application 'speculative' and an attempt to 'warehouse' orbital altitudes between 500 km and 2,000 km to block competitors.
key_facts.excerpt: On March 6, 2026, Amazon filed a formal objection to SpaceX's million-satellite plan, calling the application 'speculative' and an attempt to 'warehouse' orbital altitudes (500 km to 2,000 km) to block competitors.

stories.headline: Amazon Acquires Swiss Robotics Startup Rivr to Deploy Legged Delivery Robots Alongside Drivers

key_facts.fact: Amazon acquired Zurich-based autonomous robotics startup Rivr during the week of March 17–21, 2026. Deal terms were not disclosed. Rivr had raised $25 million in total funding and was last valued at approximately $100 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The acquisition of the Zurich-based autonomous robotics startup took place earlier this week, but the terms of the deal have not been disclosed. To date, Rivr has raised a total of $25 million and was last valued at around $100 million.

key_facts.fact: Rivr developed a four-legged robot mounted on wheels — described by cofounder and CEO Marko Bjelonic as a 'dog on roller skates' — with a cargo box on top, designed to navigate steps, curbs, and narrow pathways that wheeled-only robots cannot handle.
key_facts.excerpt: Rivr has developed a four-legged robot mounted on wheels, which was described by cofounder and CEO Marko Bjelonic as a 'dog on roller skates.'

key_facts.fact: The intended use is a cooperative delivery model: a human driver drops a parcel at one address while the Rivr robot simultaneously handles a delivery nearby, compressing stop time without eliminating the driver from the equation.
key_facts.excerpt: A human driver drops a parcel at one address while the River robot simultaneously handles a delivery nearby, compressing the time each stop takes without removing the driver from the equation entirely.

key_facts.fact: Amazon had participated in Rivr's 2024 seed funding round. Rivr had previously partnered with Just Eat Takeaway and VHO before catching Amazon's attention.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier, Amazon had participated in Rivr's 2024 seed funding round.

key_facts.fact: The acquisition extends Amazon's decade-long robotics strategy beyond warehouse automation into last-mile delivery, following its landmark 2012 purchase of Kiva Systems for $775 million.
key_facts.excerpt: This acquisition fits Amazon's decade-long robotics strategy, following its 2012 purchase of Kiva Systems, and signals expansion from warehouse automation to last-mile delivery automation.

stories.headline: Havoc AI's 3D-Printed Autonomous Vessel Harbinger Completes Maiden Voyage After 30-Day Build

key_facts.fact: Havoc AI confirmed on March 21 that its Harbinger autonomous low-profile vessel (ALPV) completed its maiden full-power voyage, marking the first operational demonstration of the platform designed for contested logistics and autonomous resupply in maritime environments.
key_facts.excerpt: Havoc AI has confirmed that its Harbinger autonomous low-profile vessel (ALPV) has completed its maiden full-power voyage, marking the initial operational demonstration of a platform developed through an accelerated design and manufacturing process.

key_facts.fact: The Harbinger was designed, manufactured, integrated, and launched in under 30 days. The hull was 3D-printed and delivered within nine days by manufacturing partner Haddy, using industrial-scale printing systems supplied by the CEAD Group.
key_facts.excerpt: The Harbinger was designed, manufactured, integrated, and launched in under 30 days, demonstrating a compressed production model enabled by large-format additive manufacturing. The hull was printed and delivered within nine days by manufacturing partner Haddy, using industrial-scale printing systems supplied by the CEAD Group.

key_facts.fact: The current Harbinger is a subscale testbed at 50–60% of full-scale design (approximately 40 feet), with the full-scale version projected at 66–80 feet. It is a semi-submersible low-draft platform designed to minimize visual and radar signatures for covert operations.
key_facts.excerpt: The vessel is intended for contested logistics and autonomous resupply missions in maritime environments.

key_facts.fact: During a two-week field exercise, operators remotely assigned tasks including autonomous navigation, resupply execution, cargo unloading, and undetected return transit. The vessel runs on Havoc AI's Havoc Stack software framework for collaborative autonomy.
key_facts.excerpt: The vessel is intended for contested logistics and autonomous resupply missions in maritime environments.

sources.title: Havoc AI's Harbinger Autonomous Vessel Completes Maiden Voyage Following 30-Day Production Cycle

stories.headline: KEWAZO Raises $35M Led by Schooner Capital for Industrial LIFTBOT Robotics Platform

key_facts.fact: KEWAZO announced a $35 million funding milestone on March 21, led by Schooner Capital and backed by Chevron Technology Ventures, Asahi Kasei, Benson Capital, Mana Ventures, Gaingels, Atlas Ventures, and existing investors True Ventures and Cybernetix Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: KEWAZO, the robotics company shaking up heavy industry, has announced a $35 million funding milestone, led by Schooner Capital and backed by Chevron Technology Ventures, Asahi Kasei, Benson Capital, Mana Ventures, Gaingels, Atlas Ventures, and existing investors True Ventures and Cybernetix Ventures.

key_facts.fact: KEWAZO's flagship LIFTBOT is deployed at more than 20 industrial sites across North America and Europe, including refineries, petrochemical plants, chemical complexes, and power facilities, replacing cranes and manual handling to boost safety and efficiency.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's flagship LIFTBOT is already hard at work at more than 20 industrial sites across North America and Europe, including refineries, petrochemical plants, chemical complexes, and power facilities. By replacing cranes and manual handling, LIFTBOT is boosting safety, efficiency, and schedule predictability.

key_facts.fact: With LIFTBOT collecting structured operational data from high-barrier industrial environments, KEWAZO is building a Physical AI platform aimed at bringing transparency today and automation tomorrow. CEO Artem Kuchukov said KEWAZO helps 'industrial asset owners adopt automation by delivering instant value in vertical material movement.'
key_facts.excerpt: With LIFTBOT on site, KEWAZO collects structured operational data from high-barrier industrial environments—a foundation for its Physical AI platform, which aims to bring transparency today and automation tomorrow.

stories.headline: Russia Launches Progress MS-33 Cargo Ship to ISS From Repaired Baikonur Pad

key_facts.fact: A Soyuz-2.1a carrier rocket carrying the Progress MS-33 resupply ship successfully lifted off from Baikonur Cosmodrome on March 22, 2026, toward the International Space Station. The spacecraft separated from the upper stage and entered its designated orbit approximately nine minutes after liftoff.
key_facts.excerpt: A Soyuz-2.1a carrier rocket with the Progress MS-33 resupply ship successfully lifted off from the Baikonur spaceport towards the International Space Station.

key_facts.fact: Progress MS-33 is carrying 2,509 kg of useful cargo to the ISS, including 1,211 kg of dry cargo (with Sun-Terahertz scientific equipment), 828 kg of propellant for station refueling, 420 liters of potable water, and 50 kg of oxygen for atmosphere replenishment.
key_facts.excerpt: The Progress MS-33 resupply ship will deliver 2,509 kg of useful cargo to the ISS, including 1,211 kg of dry cargo.

key_facts.fact: Docking with the Poisk module of the ISS Russian segment is expected on March 24 at 4:35 p.m. Moscow time (1:35 p.m. GMT), after an approximately 49.5-hour transit.
key_facts.excerpt: Its docking with the Poisk module of the Russian segment of the International Space Station is expected at 4:35 p.m. Moscow time (1:35 p.m. GMT) on March 24.

key_facts.fact: The launch took place from a pad at Baikonur that had been repaired after the Soyuz MS-28 launch in late November 2025 caused severe damage to the facility, making this the first launch from the restored pad.
key_facts.excerpt: Just under four months after Soyuz MS-28 launched from Site 31/6 at Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, an eventful flight that resulted in severe damage.

stories.headline: US Space Force Switches GPS III-8 Launch From Troubled Vulcan Centaur to SpaceX Falcon 9

key_facts.fact: The U.S. Space Force announced it is shifting the GPS III-8 satellite launch from United Launch Alliance's Vulcan Centaur rocket to SpaceX's Falcon 9, due to ongoing solid rocket booster anomalies detected on Vulcan Centaur during two of its four flights since its January 2024 debut.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Space Force has announced a change in plans for its upcoming GPS III-8 satellite launch, shifting the mission to SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket due to ongoing technical issues with the Vulcan Centaur rocket.

key_facts.fact: Col. Ryan Hiserote, commander of Space Systems Command System Delta 80, said: 'With this change, we are answering the call for rapid delivery of advanced GPS capability while the Vulcan anomaly investigation continues.' The launch is now targeted for no earlier than late April 2026 from Cape Canaveral.
key_facts.excerpt: 'With this change, we are answering the call for rapid delivery of advanced GPS capability while the Vulcan anomaly investigation continues', said Col. Ryan Hiserote, commander of Space Systems Command System Delta 80.

key_facts.fact: GPS III-8 is the tenth and final spacecraft in the GPS III series. The Space Force had paused all national security launches on Vulcan Centaur in February to investigate the SRB anomalies, which occurred during the certification flight in October 2024 and the USSF-87 mission last month.
key_facts.excerpt: Vulcan Centaur, ULA's next-generation rocket and successor to the Atlas V, has experienced SRB-related issues during two of its four launches since debuting in January 2024. These anomalies occurred during Vulcan's national security payload certification flight in October 2024 and, most recently, during the USSF-87 mission last month.

sources.title: US Space Force moves GPS III satellite launch to SpaceX Falcon 9
